outline.chapter_title: 1. Introduction to Text‑to‑Image Diffusion and Finetuning Challenges
outline.description: Sets the stage by explaining the rise of diffusion models, why fine‑grained control is needed, and the specific downstream tasks considered.
subtopics: Overview of modern diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, Imagen, etc.)
Limitations of text prompts for fine‑control
Subject‑driven generation: definition & motivation
Controllable generation: definition & motivation
Desiderata for an effective finetuning strategy (efficiency & generalizability)
outline.description: Provides the theoretical and empirical foundations that motivate orthogonal finetuning, and surveys prior approaches to subject‑driven and controllable generation as well as generic finetuning techniques.
subtopics: Citation of ground‑breaking text‑to‑image diffusion papers
Explanation of latent vs pixel space diffusion techniques
Review of subject‑driven methods ( DreamBooth, LoRA, Attention adapters )
Review of controllable generation methods (ControlNet, T2I‑Adapter)
Survey of generic model adaptation techniques (LoRA, adapters, orthogonal training)
outline.description: Explains why preserving neuron directions (angles) matters for semantic retention and why an orthogonal transformation is a principled way to realize this intuition.
subtopics: The role of neuron angles vs magnitudes in deep nets – SphereNet, angular similarity studies
Toy experiment with convolution autoencoder demonstrating angle importance
Why global rotation/reflection preserves pairwise angles – orthogonal matrices as rotations/reflections
Comparison to low‑rank LoRA updates – flexibility vs structural regularity
outline.chapter_title: 4. Hyperspherical Energy and its Invariance Property
outline.description: Defines hyperspherical energy, explains its connection to semantic preservation, and shows that orthogonal transformations keep it invariant.
subtopics: Definition of hyperspherical similarity and energy for a weight matrix
Interpretation of hyperspherical energy as neuron uniformity on unit sphere
Empirical evidence that low energy correlates with semantic preservation in diffusion models
Mathematical proof of invariance under orthogonal transformations
outline.chapter_title: 5. Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) – Formalism and Algorithmic Details
outline.description: Presents the formal optimization formulation for OFT, how orthogonal matrices are parameterized and learned, and practical training considerations.
subtopics: Optimization objective: minimize energy difference → orthogonality constraint
Parameterizing layer‑shared orthogonal matrices (Cayley transform)
Block‑diagonal structure for parameter efficiency and convolution compatibility
Initializing R as identity to preserve pretrained weights
Guaranteeing orthogonality with differentiable constraints (QR / Cayley)
outline.description: Describes two practical variants that improve stability or flexibility beyond vanilla OFT.
subtopics: Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT): epsilon deviation from identity; enforcing via projected gradient on Q matrix; effect on convergence stability
subtopics2: Re‑scaled OFT: adding a learnable diagonal scaling matrix D so magnitudes are adjusted without changing energy; theoretical motivation
outline.description: Delves into deeper properties of OFT such as computational complexity, comparison to LoRA, convergence behavior, inference overhead.|

outline: Complexity analysis: parameter count O(d^2/r) with block diagonal; comparison to LoRA O(d^2+dn)
Trade‐off between flexibility and regularity: rigid rotations vs uncontrolled gradient updates; why OFT converges faster
No extra inference cost: pre-multiply R into W0 during inference
Potential extensions: compositionality via multiplication of multiple OFT matrices
description: Shows how OFT is integrated with DreamBooth pipeline for subject preservation tasks, detailing experimental setup and quantitative/qualitative results.
subtopics: Experiment protocol: Stable Diffusion v1.5 + DreamBooth loss setup
Baselines comparison: DreamBooth vs LoRA vs OFT/COFT
Finetuning stability charts across epochs
Quantitative metrics: CLIP-I, DINO, LPIPS
Qualitative comparisons: identity preservation vs text fidelity
Human evaluation insights
description: Illustrates usage on edge/segmentation/landmark conditioning tasks; introduces new control consistency metrics; presents comparative outcomes.
subtopics: Task definitions: Canny→Image, Segmentation→Image, Landmark→Face
Benchmark datasets COCO/ADE20K/CelebA-HQ
Baseline methods: ControlNet, T2I‑Adapter, LoRA
Fast convergence evidence via landmark error curves
Control consistency metrics per task (IoU/F1/accuracy/l2)
Quantitative results table
Qualitative sample comparisons

description: Summarizes open challenges highlighted by authors and suggests possible research avenues.
subtopics: Scalability of Cayley’s inverse operation; differentiable fast approximations
Compositionality potential – combining multiple OFT transforms
Block diagonal bias vs full orthogonal matrix – parameter efficiency trade‑offs
Extending OFT beyond latent diffusion layers (e.g., cross‑attention)
